issues.claim: R4-04 (b) makes every reader of a disaster look's damage, tone, lines and rows read one predicate: the look stands over a building of its units until V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` turns true on it (base §10.2 (f)). §8.2 keeps a unit's `ruinTone` only 'while the look stands over any of its buildings', and V09's why card on a building shows `info.crisis.ruinedFor` only where `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` is true (§11.2). V07 §4.5's crisis line, rewritten this round, gives that row 'for a `VillageEnd` a disaster look ruins … while a crisis look stands at the viewer's key', read from `opts.view`'s `crises`, `week` and `looks`: that is the look's weeks, with no hand-over. V07 §5.6 (4) has the ruined look yield building by building to its rebuild's Works. So an end whose every building has begun its rebuild inside the condition's weeks draws no ruined tone and no building row, yet its own why card says 'For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34'. This is two outcomes for one case, R4-04's class, which it graded major. R4-04's sweep did not list V07 §4.5, §5.6 (6) or T-V7-69 (e), and bar (e) passes the stale row.
issues.required_change: V07 §4.5's crisis line: 'the answer for a `VillageEnd` a disaster look ruins and for a `VillageField` a famine look leaves bare carries' → 'the answer for a `VillageEnd` of a disaster look's units (§10.2 (d)) while the look stands over a building on its plots (`villageUnitPlots`; §10.2 (f): V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` not yet true on it at `opts.view`'s week, a preview never handing over — as the end's `ruinTone` stands, §8.2) and for a `VillageField` a famine look leaves bare carries'. W74's input cell adds 'V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` on the end's buildings (`villageUnitPlots`) for the crisis line'. V07 §5.6 (6): 'carries the crisis line on a ruined end and a bare field' → 'carries the crisis line on an end the disaster look stands over (§10.2 (f)) and on a bare field'. T-V7-69 (e): 'on an end a disaster look ruins' → 'on an end of a disaster look's units', and after 'and none otherwise' add ', an end every building of which has begun its rebuild's Works (the look standing over none of them, its `ruinTone` gone) among the none'.

issues.claim: R4-04's two phrases are missing at three other V07 sites. Each is a restatement narrower in form; V07 §5.6 (3) defines the units and V06 §3.22 (3) and §8.2 are cited, so nothing built changes. (1) §5.6 (3)'s **The look** says 'a building whose rebuild Works has begun draws its Works instead (V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields`)'. That names only a rebuild and omits the predicate's 'other than a `decay` Works', 'unless finished before the overlay's `sinceWeek`' and 'a preview never hands over'. It also gives the units' tone without 'while the look stands over any of its buildings'. (2) §5.6 (5) says 'the ruined ends' tone'. (3) §3.17's row 'a crisis look over a hand-off epoch' says 'the village's ends after a hand-off down'. Both use 'ends' alone at the village rungs, where an end-less thorp's units are its toft groups (R4-04 (a)).
issues.required_change: V07 §5.6 (3) **The look**: 'Every building on a returned unit's plots draws item 123's damage at `lookLevel` by severity, or at its own decay level where that is higher (V02's exterior, V03's plan; nothing stored), and the unit's plots' faces take §8.2's ruined tone at the city band; a building whose rebuild Works has begun draws its Works instead (V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields`).' → 'Every building on a returned unit's plots draws item 123's damage at `lookLevel` by severity, or at its own decay level where that is higher (V02's exterior, V03's plan; nothing stored), while the look stands over it (§10.2 (f): until V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` turns true on it, then its Works; a preview never handing over), and the unit's plots' faces take §8.2's ruined tone at the city band while the look stands over any of its buildings.' §5.6 (5): 'the ruined ends' tone' → 'the ruined units' tone ((3))'. §3.17's row 'a crisis look over a hand-off epoch': 'the village's ends after a hand-off down' → 'V07 §5.6 (3)'s units (its ends, or an end-less thorp's toft groups) after a hand-off down'.

issues.claim: V08 §3.5's new absorb rule (R4-15 (a)) holds the carried fact for 'a field that takes its field-table fallback (V08 §2.4) — its path absent, or its value of no form its row reads'. The field table routes record sub-fields through the same fallback cells. The `institutions[]` row says 'a record's own absent field takes its row's `else` (V08 §2.6)', and its paths list `status`, `inactive`, `worldPulseFate`, `remnantReason` and `impairments[]`. The `activeConditions[]` row says 'a missing `label` no name, a missing `duration` no `untilWeek`, a missing `sourceEventType` the `archetype` row'. The rule does not say whether it reaches inside a record. Read literally, an institution whose record drops a current-only stamp keeps its carried `fate` and `inactive`; SettlementForge's entity stamps (`worldPulseFate`, `remnantReason`, the `…ByEventId` stamps) are 'per entity, current only' (research/sf/dossier-generation.md l. 864). With the diff's 'fates first' (§3.5's institution row; §7.7 item 14), a record SettlementForge reopens (F6: 'status back to `active`', research/sf/mapping.md l. 628) then stays closed on the map. Its cleared impairments and a condition's dropped `duration` also stay as carried. Read as top-level paths only, the record's `else` is compared as before round 4 and the institution reopens. Two builders build different absorbs on the reopen path. R4-15 (a)'s reason ('on a map made without a dossier nothing moves the population, the name, the tier or the institutions') concerns the dossier's own fields, not a readable record's optional parts.
issues.required_change: V08 §3.5's diff, after '— makes no change: the carried fact stands.': add 'A field here is a row's own path — a top-level key, or a whole list; inside a record the digest reads (an institution, power, notable, condition, calamity or tradition), a sub-field absent or unreadable takes its row's reading (an institution field's `else`, V08 §2.6; the `activeConditions[]` row's missing `label`, `duration` and `sourceEventType`) at an absorb as at a creation and is compared as read, so a record follows what the dossier now says of it (an institution SettlementForge reopens, `status` `active` and its `worldPulseFate` gone, reopens, F6).' V08 §2.4's table lead: 'at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing,' → 'at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing — a row's own path; a record's absent or unreadable sub-field is read by its row and compared (V08 §3.5) —,'. T-V8-61 (a) adds: 'an absorb on `town-1` whose ruined or remnant institution record returns with `status` `active` and no `worldPulseFate` reopens it (F6), and one whose condition drops `duration` clears its `untilWeek`'.

issues.claim: Round 4 made a late arrival a defined case for a calamity only (V08 §3.6 (3) under R4-08; T-V8-49 (g)). Its F5 targets' dossier events 'ride that epoch with it', with no week stated; the calamity's own entry sits at `W₀` + 1. Every other newly carried element change dated at or before `W₀`, in an absorb whose `W₁` is after `W₀`, has no stated week. §3.6 (6) folds element events 'at their week, between the epochs of (3)', but such a week lies before the last epoch, which is already in the log. §7.7 item 6 has the change mutate 'the map the last epoch left', and §4.11 *The clock* (1) takes the document's current week from 'the last folded event that carries one'. So an absorb whose last event is such a change (its present week coming from a tick already carried) moves the drawn week back before the last epoch: the season and every Works stage begun since then are drawn as of an earlier week. The degenerate row (`W₁` not after `W₀`) applies such changes finished. The case where `W₁` is after `W₀` has no outcome and no test (principle (11)).
issues.required_change: V08 §3.6 (6), after 'undated ones follow the last epoch, applied finished (no Works).': add 'A newly carried change dated at or before the last epoch's week `W₀` folds after the last epoch at `W₀` + 1, applied finished (no Works), its own tick kept in its receipt and noted by `unreceipted_change`'s `late` variant — never at a week before the last epoch's, so §4.11 *The clock* (1)'s current week never falls back; a late calamity's F5 targets' dossier events ride that calamity's epoch in its `EpochInputs.dossier` at `W₀` + 1 ((3)).' V08 §3.6 (3)'s calamities parenthesis: 'its F5 targets' dossier events riding that epoch with it, above' → 'its F5 targets' dossier events riding that epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` with it at `W₀` + 1, (6)'. V08 §4.6's `unreceipted_change` row: 'for a calamity carried at or before the last epoch's week by an absorb whose week is not after it (V08 §3.6 (3); V08 §3.17)' → 'for a change carried at or before the last epoch's week (V08 §3.6 (3), (6); V08 §3.17)'. §3.17's 'changes to events and epochs' row adds to its degenerate inputs: 'a newly carried non-calamity change dated at or before `W₀`, `W₁` after it: folded at `W₀` + 1, applied finished, noted `late`'. T-V8-49 (g) adds that case, asserting that the document's current week after the absorb is not before `W₀`.

issues.claim: V08 ## 6's catch-up batch row has three imprecisions in its new text. (a) The batch is 'the dossier events one epoch's span holds — dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week]', but an event dated at the epoch's own week rides that epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` (V08 §3.6 (6); §7.7 item 6) and is never a standalone event of the pass. (b) 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms and ≤ 3.5 ms' leaves the rung of each implicit; V06 §6.8 (1) states it (3 ms at TOWN and CITY, 3.5 ms at METROPOLIS). (c) 'one of T-V6-24's fixtures doing so fails the release' can be read to include T-V6-24's fourth catch-up fixture (100 years carrying 5 000 at the METROPOLIS cap). That fixture is built to pass the budget, and its bar is the one-epoch fold reported F-BUDGET-TIME; V06 §6.8 (6) says 'one of T-V6-24's three catch-up fixtures'. Each point is cited to the text that settles it.
issues.required_change: V08 ## 6's 'an absorb with epochs' row: (a) 'dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week]' → 'dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week) — one dated at the epoch's own week riding its `EpochInputs.dossier` (V08 §3.6 (6))'; (b) 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms and ≤ 3.5 ms, averaged' → 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms at TOWN and CITY and ≤ 3.5 ms at the METROPOLIS cap, averaged'; (c) 'one of T-V6-24's fixtures doing so fails the release' → 'one of those three fixtures doing so fails the release (T-V6-24's over-budget fixture, 100 years carrying 5 000 at the cap, takes that one-epoch fold reported F-BUDGET-TIME by design)'.

Two restatements of the `name` fallback still give only the creation value. §5.5 says 'an empty dossier name takes the generator's own (§10.4; V08 §2.4's fallback, noted `field_fallback`), so a title always has one'. §3.17's labels row says 'an empty dossier name takes the generator's own (§10.4), noted `field_fallback`'. issues.claim: VV1112-r3-03's fixture sentence (V08 §7.1) stands the three crises' shared week 'on `city-1` and on `metropolis-3`'. V12 §3.15.12's T122-6 and X-V12-5 measure that week 'at CITY and at the METROPOLIS cap'. `metropolis-3` is a frozen METROPOLIS fixture of 45 824 people (research/sf/PLAN.md l. 406), not the 120 000 cap. Elsewhere V08 keeps the two apart: its force fixtures stand 'each at TOWN, CITY and the METROPOLIS cap', and §3.17 tests 'the cap's 120 000'. So the share under `densityCap` is measured at the cap on no fixture.
issues.required_change: V08 §7.1's fixtures sentence: 'with one week on `city-1` and on `metropolis-3` in which' → 'with one week on `city-1` and on `metropolis-3` with its population raised to the 120 000 cap (a test-side mutation in §13.2's frozen manifest, as the force fixtures' cap) in which'.
